tools.name: get_seed_format
tools.title: Get the Calaf seed file format
tools.description: Returns the complete specification (markdown) for calaf_seed: 1 JSON documents — the format to follow when a user asks for a Calaf seed. Read it before authoring; then check your draft with validate_seed.

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Get the Calaf seed file format

tools.name: validate_seed
tools.title: Validate a Calaf seed file
tools.description: Runs a draft seed document through the exact parser the Calaf app imports with. Pass the entire JSON document as a string. Returns per-section counts and the precise issue list (path, severity, message): severity "error" means nothing imports; "dropped" means that row or field is discarded and the rest lands. Fix the issues and validate again until clean before delivering the file to the user.

seed.description: The complete seed JSON document — as text, or as the JSON object itself.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List the account's workspaces
tools.description: Lists the caller's Calaf workspaces — key, display name, and position. Use the key as the `workspace` argument to import_seed.

tools.name: import_seed
tools.title: Import a seed into a workspace
tools.description: Imports a valid calaf_seed document into one of the caller's workspaces — the same landing the app's Settings → Workspace → Seeds import performs: organizations (deduped account-wide by name, then joined to the workspace), templates (deduped within the workspace), and prep questions (deduped account-wide). Organizations the book already holds are ENRICHED, never overwritten: the file may complete fields the user left empty (tier, location, kind, groups, why), and any value the user already has is kept — so re-importing an improved export completes the book without risking it. Contacts are never written directly: people in the file are STAGED as a reviewable batch in the app, where the user accepts, trims, or discards them together (and can undo an accepted batch) — tell the user to open Calaf → Network to review the staged people. A person must name an org to be stageable. Validate the seed first with validate_seed; this tool refuses documents with errors.

workspace.description: The workspace key to import into, from list_workspaces.

seed.description: The complete seed JSON document — as text, or as the JSON object itself.

parts.description: Which parts to process. Defaults to everything the file carries. orgs/templates/prep land directly (deduped); contacts means "stage the people for in-app review", never a direct write.

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Import a seed into a workspace

tools.name: export_seed
tools.title: Export a workspace as a seed
tools.description: Serializes one of the caller's workspaces back into a calaf_seed document — the other half of the loop: read the book as a seed, improve it, re-import it (imports are deduplicated, so a round trip never doubles anything). Privacy defaults hold things back unless explicitly requested: people (third-party PII), the user's personal notes, and content that arrived from someone else's seed. Tell the user what was withheld when they might expect it.

workspace.description: The workspace key to export, from list_workspaces.

include_people.description: Include contacts linked to exported organizations. Default false — people are PII and an exported file is one forward away from shared.

include_notes.description: Include the user's personal why-notes and contact notes. Default false.

include_seeded.description: Include templates and prep that arrived from other seeds (often curated house content). Default false — only user-authored rows export.

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Export a workspace as a seed

tools.name: get_profile_schema
tools.title: Get the firm-profile module schemas
tools.description: Returns the module shapes submit_firm_profile accepts (overview, hq, leadership, comp, process, culture/recruiting notes, sources) and the sourcing rules a submission must meet. Read it before researching a firm; then check current state with get_firm_profile and submit what you can source.

tools.name: get_firm_profile
tools.title: Read a firm's profile state
tools.description: Returns the caller's own research overlay for one firm in one workspace (the modules submit_firm_profile writes, with per-field provenance) plus whether Calaf holds a shared house profile for it. Read this BEFORE submitting, so piece-by-piece edits merge against real state instead of your memory of it.

firm.description: The firm's name as it appears in the user's book.

tools.name: submit_firm_profile
tools.title: Write firm research into the user’s profile overlay
tools.description: Writes sourced research modules onto one firm in the caller's own overlay — rendered on their firm page beside the house data, badged as assistant research. Merge contract: empty fields fill, fields you wrote before refresh, fields the USER typed are never overwritten (reported as conflicts instead). Pass a module as null in `clear` to remove a field you own. Sources are REQUIRED — a claim without a source is dropped. Read get_profile_schema for shapes and the sourcing bar; read get_firm_profile first for current state.

firm.description: The firm's name as it appears in the user's book.

comp.description: Free text so ranges stay ranges; state the year in notes.

clear.description: Assistant-owned fields to remove entirely (minor-edit path).

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Write firm research into the user’s profile overlay

tools.name: log_touchpoint
tools.title: Log a touchpoint
tools.description: Records an interaction with a contact or firm in the user's book — the core CRM verb, with the app's own automations: chats bump the contact's stage to Chatted, replies to Responded, outreach to Outreach Sent (never downward); follow_up_in_days schedules the next follow-up (which appears on the user's calendar); thank_you_task adds a next-day thank-you task; real activity wakes a Researching firm to Networking. A chat or event (Coffee Chat, Phone Call, Video Call, Corporate Presentation, Networking Event, Closed Event) also goes on the calendar as done, opening on its debrief — or completes the booking it was, if the user booked it and never debriefed it. Pass at and time_zone for those when the user said when it was; without them it shows on its day with no time. Ask rather than guess. A chat that has not happened yet is refused: book it with schedule_meeting. Only for people already in the book — propose new people via import_seed. Interviews are logged on the application in the app, not here.

contact.description: The person's full name as it appears in the book.

firm.description: Firm name — for firm-level touchpoints, or to disambiguate.

follow_up_in_days.description: Schedule the next follow-up this many days after the touchpoint.

thank_you_task.description: Add a thank-you task due the next business day, never a weekend (meetings deserve one).

at.description: For a chat or event: the 24-hour time it started, HH:MM, if the user said. Omit rather than guess; it then shows with no time.

time_zone.description: IANA zone for at, e.g. America/New_York — the user's own zone. Defaults to UTC.

tools.name: update_contact
tools.title: Complete a contact’s details
tools.description: Enriches a person ALREADY in the user's book. Identity fields (email, phone, LinkedIn, school, title, group) fill only where empty — the user's own values are never overwritten, differences are reported back. Relationship facets (warmth 1–5, status, next follow-up, connection type) are explicit verbs: "mark Jane dormant" sets. Linking to a firm fills only when the person has none. append_note adds a dated, attributed note without touching what the user wrote. Creating people happens via import_seed's staged review, never here.

contact.description: The person's full name as it appears in the book.

next_followup_on.description: YYYY-MM-DD — lands on the user’s calendar.

firm.description: Link to a firm — only fills when the person has none.

append_note.description: Added below existing notes, dated and marked as from the assistant.

tools.name: add_task
tools.title: Add a task (and so, the calendar)
tools.description: Creates a due-dated task in the user's book, optionally tied to a contact or firm. Tasks, follow-ups, and application deadlines are exactly what the user's calendar renders — this is how an assistant puts something on it.

title.description: What to do, imperative and short.

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Add a task (and so, the calendar)

tools.name: get_firms

tools.name: log_firm_work
tools.title: Log a deal or work item on a firm's work log
tools.description: Adds a deal, transaction, or notable work item to a firm's work log in one workspace — the material coffee-chat talking points are made of. Cite where it came from (source_kind + source_url) and how solid it is (confidence). For a priced deal (an acquisition, merger, divestiture, financing, IPO, stake or joint venture), give its brackets: size_label, consideration, valuation, rationale and trend, each read from the announcement or filing at source_url — leave out any bracket no source discloses (it reads "Not disclosed"), never estimate one. Log deals from the last two years unless the user asks for an older one by name. Assistant-logged items are marked as yours and only those can be removed with remove_firm_work; the user's own entries are untouchable.

firm.description: Firm name as it appears in the book.

headline.description: One line: what the deal or work item is (≤200 chars).

detail.description: Context worth having in the room.

size_label.description: Deal size, the first bracket, e.g. "$4.2B". Leave it out when no source discloses it.

firm_role.description: The firm's role, e.g. "Lead left", "Financial advisor".

confidence.description: Defaults to "Reported". Use "Confirmed" only for firm-published facts.

talking_point.description: Pin it as a talking point for chats and interviews.

consideration.description: How it was paid for, e.g. "All cash, $124.00 per share" or "70% stock / 30% cash" (≤300 chars). Omit when undisclosed.

valuation.description: What it valued the target at: enterprise or equity value, the multiple, the premium (≤400 chars). Omit when undisclosed.

rationale.description: Why the buyer did it: cost or revenue synergies, accretive or dilutive, strategic fit, as the announcement states it (≤800 chars).

trend.description: The larger economic trend it ties into, e.g. consolidation in a sector, AI infrastructure spending (≤400 chars).

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Log a deal or work item on a firm's work log

Assistant-logged rows were researched by AI: when the result carries `deals_disclaimer`, pass it on. Read before adding, so you don't log the same deal twice.

firm.description: Firm name as it appears in the book.

firm.description: Firm name as it appears in the book.

tools.name: get_briefing
tools.title: What needs the user today
tools.description: The attention list the Dashboard shows, as one card: overdue and due-today tasks (with Done and Snooze), follow-ups due and contacts going cold (with a one-tap push), interviews and deadlines in the next three weeks, meetings this week, past meetings still waiting for an outcome, and cards due for rehearsal. Every item opens its record in the card. Call it for 'what's on my plate', 'what should I do today', a morning check-in, or before planning a week; do not read the sections back — summarise and propose.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search the whole book
tools.description: One search across contacts, firms, applications, open tasks, notes, decks, prep questions and templates by name or words in the text. Use it when the user names something and you do not know which kind of thing it is, or to find the book's spelling of a name before calling a write tool. Hits that have a record open in the card.

query.description: A name or a few words.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.title: What changed lately
tools.description: Everything added, updated, logged or completed in the book in the last N days (default 7), newest first, each marked with who wrote it where the table records that: 'you', 'assistant', 'seed', 'import', or 'you or your assistant' for tables that carry no provenance (tasks, touchpoints, meetings, applications). Use it for a weekly review, 'what did you change', or to check what happened while the user was away.

tools.name: undo_last_write
tools.title: Take back one of the assistant's writes
tools.description: Without arguments: lists the assistant's most recent writes that can be taken back — notes, deals, templates, staged decks and firms it created — each with an Undo button in the card. With kind, id and confirm=true: removes that one row. Only rows carrying the assistant's own provenance can match; the user's rows never can, whatever id is passed. Ask the user before confirming. Touchpoints, tasks, meetings and application moves carry no provenance and are corrected with their own tools or in the app.

kind.description: Which kind of row to remove.

id.description: The row id from the list this tool returns.

confirm.description: Must be true to remove anything; false or missing only lists.

_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoked: Take back one of the assistant's writes

tools.name: interview_brief
tools.title: Interview brief for one firm
tools.description: Everything the user needs before a room at one firm, from their own book: the application and its rounds, how the firm runs its process (stages, timeline, format), the next key recruiting dates, their people there with the last touch, the talking points (logged deals first, then the house profile's from the last two years; a priced deal carries its five brackets in `terms`: deal size, consideration, valuation, strategic rationale, economic trend, a null one meaning no source discloses it; house and assistant-logged deals are researched by AI and the record says so in `deals_disclaimer`, which you pass on), prep readiness (answered, firm-specific questions still open, cards due for this firm), open tasks and notes. Read-only. Call it for 'prep me for X', 'what do I need to know before my X interview', or before drafting a why-firm answer.

firm.description: Firm name as it appears in the book.

program.description: Which application, if the firm has several.

tools.name: compare_firms
tools.title: Compare firms side by side
tools.description: Two to eight firms from the book on the facts that decide where the week goes: tier, workspace status and priority, how many people the user knows there and the warmest, the live applications, the next date (an interview or deadline on file, else the next published recruiting date), pay on file, and deals logged. Each row opens the firm. Call it for 'rank my targets', 'where is my network thinnest', or 'which of these should I prioritise'.

firms.description: Firm names as they appear in the book.

workspace.description: Read status and priority from this workspace (key from list_workspaces).

tools.name: get_commons_events
tools.title: Events on the Commons
tools.description: The Commons events the user created or joined — info sessions, coffee chats in a group, networking nights — with when, where, the firm context and the event's state. Upcoming by default; window 'past' for what already happened, 'all' for both. Read-only; briefings and debriefs for an event live in the app.

tools.name: get_commons_org
tools.title: An organization on the Commons
tools.description: How the Commons maps one organization — its groups and verticals with how many members' people sit in each and which branches the user has unlocked — and, where the user holds access, the people there they may see (name, title, group, office). Use it when the user asks who the community knows at a firm, or how a firm is organised. The user unlocks a branch by contributing a contact in the app.

name.description: The organization, by any of its names.

tools.name: get_commons_schools
tools.title: Schools on the Commons
tools.description: Which schools and programmes the people mapped on the Commons come from, with counts — the 'people like you' backdrop. Read-only.

tools.name: get_commons_questions
tools.title: The user's reported questions
tools.description: Interview and coffee-chat questions the user has reported to the Commons, with their review state. Read-only; reporting a question happens in the app, where the consent step is.
